name: Akseli Gallen-Kallela
bio: Akseli Gallen-Kallela was a Finnish painter and a leading figure of Finnish romantic nationalism around the turn of the 20th century. He is considered a pioneer of a distinctly Finnish national art, and his work is regarded as a very important aspect of Finnish national identity.

paintings.title: Lemminkäinen's Mother
paintings.story: Lemminkäinen's Mother is an 1897 Romantic nationalist painting by Finnish painter Akseli Gallen-Kallela. The painting illustrates a passage from the Kalevala, the Finnish national epic compiled by Elias Lönnrot in the 19th century.

paintings.title: Saunassa
paintings.story: Saunassa is an 1889 oil painting by the Finnish artist Akseli Gallen-Kallela. It was painted in Ekola's croft in Keuruu. Gallen-Kallela gave his work to Knut Tilgmann, whose brother gave it to Ateneum in 1922. Gallen-Kallela did not like the picture and thought that it was unfinished.

paintings.title: The Defense of the Sampo
paintings.story: The Defense of the Sampo is a tempera-on-canvas Romantic national painting created in 1896 by Finnish painter Akseli Gallen-Kallela. The painting illustrates a passage from the Kalevala, the Finnish national epic compiled by Elias Lönnrot in the 19th century.
facts: The painting was originally commissioned by a wealthy patron from Helsinki, Salomo Wuorio, for his dining room.
When the painting was first exhibited, it received widespread attention and was considered to be Gallen-Kallela's finest work.

paintings.title: Parisian Backyard
paintings.story: Parisian Backyard is an oil-on-canvas painting executed in 1884 by Finnish artist Akseli Gallen-Kallela. The work is 28 × 23 cm in size and belongs to the Ateneum, part of the Finnish National Gallery in Helsinki, where it was donated in 1945.
facts: The Parisian Backyard is a work of Gallen-Kallela's first trip to Paris, in the autumn of 1884.
There he painted some academic works as part of his studies, as well as other paintings such as the Parisian Backyard.

paintings.title: Kullervo Sets Off for War
paintings.story: Kullervo Sets Off for War is a painting by Akseli Gallen-Kallela from the year 1901. He painted the subject in tempera painting and as a fresco which is located in the music hall of Old Student House of Helsinki University.
facts: The fresco was donated to the Students' union by Otto Donner.
The theme for the painting is from the Kalevala, national epic of Finland.

paintings.title: Symposium (Gallen-Kallela)
paintings.story: Symposium is an oil painting created by Akseli Gallen-Kallela in 1894.
facts: After the painting became exhibited most of the Finnish audience and critics did not approve of it and the artist suffered public disapproval.
The rest of the Symposium circle were also criticised for leading questionable lives.

paintings.title: The Artist's Mother
paintings.story: This is the artist’s mother in a remarkable, enigmatic portrait. Intimate and monumental at the same time. On the one hand a spitting image, on the other a sculpture in a dreamlike landscape seemingly situated beyond time and space. The portrait is dated 1896, the year before Akseli Gallen-Kallela cast her as the main figure in one of his most famous paintings, Lemminkäinen’s Mother – a motif inspired by Finland’s national epic, Kalevala.

paintings.title: Regent Mannerheim's batman Gustaf Hagenau
paintings.story: Portrait of Gustaf Hagenau, a colour sergeant and Swedish citizen who served as Mannerheim’s valet. The portrait shows Hagenau in uniform decorated with the Cross of Liberty, 4th Class, the Medal of Liberty, 2nd Class, the Swedish His Majesty’s The King’s Medal and the Danish Royal Medal of Recompense. Hagenau received the First Class Medal of the White Rose of Finland on the 18th of June, 1919, not seen in this portrait.
